quotes.text: [Checkout studio (Private preview)](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/checkout-studio.md): Launch, configure, and monitor Checkout integrations from the Dashboard without writing code.
We recommend the Checkout Sessions API for most integrations.
When you use this API, you calculate the final amount and manage the entire checkout lifecycle in your own code.
Your customers can save their credit cards, debit cards, or US bank accounts for faster checkout at any Link-enabled business.

old_evidence.text: Stripe recommends using the Checkout Sessions API with the Payment Element over Payment Intents for most integrations.
Before you get started, you must [register for a Stripe account](https://dashboard.stripe.com/register).
Use Mobile Elements to accept payments in iOS and Android apps.
Create, customize, and send invoices from the Dashboard.

findings: November is a full overview of Optimized Checkout Suite payments UIs, dynamic payment methods and Link. It retains Payment Links for no-code acceptance without a website, positions a prebuilt full page (embedded or redirected on the merchant website) as recommended, gives a distinct embedded-form route, lists custom Elements and Mobile Payment Element for iOS, Android and React Native, and labels Dashboard Checkout studio Private preview. The April overview covered hosted/embedded Checkout, Elements, Payment Links and iOS/Android and explicitly required Stripe account signup (old raw lines 8–20, new raw lines 5–27).

Both captures prefer Checkout Sessions for most integrations, with November expanding the comparison. Checkout Sessions can use `price_data` for basic collection or line items, address collection, tax, discounts, shipping, subscriptions, order details, dynamic inventory/line-item updates and Adaptive Pricing for fuller flows. `automatic_tax.enabled=true` enables Stripe Tax in the stated example; PaymentIntents offers lower-level control and merchant ownership of final amount and checkout lifecycle, requiring separately integrated tax and subscriptions and merchant-written discounts, shipping, address/order tracking, currency conversion and amount updates. Adaptive Pricing is a Checkout Sessions product feature, not established for PaymentIntents just because currency conversion can be built separately (old raw line 8, new raw lines 29–62).

November's comparison describes Checkout Session expiration at 24 hours and full lifecycle events versus PaymentIntent payment-status events and no automatic Session expiration. The separate November Checkout Sessions create API gives 24-hour default with configurable `expires_at` 30 minutes to 24 hours after creation. The separate Checkout Session object distinguishes `status=complete` with possible payment processing from `payment_status` for fulfillment. No table entry authorizes fulfillment, proves receipt or funding, or describes an exhaustive list of account event types (new raw lines 59–62; related Checkout API create lines 316–317 and object lines 312–322, 368–378; mapped source lines 34–45, 54–62).

November adds consumer/merchant routing topics: dynamic payment methods display/order, scenarios via method configurations, availability rules, Dashboard A/B testing, and a Private preview Checkout studio method-management route. Link can reuse saved credit/debit cards and U.S. bank accounts across Link-enabled businesses and names Instant Bank Payments and Klarna. The overview links Checkout, Web Elements and native iOS/Android/React Native Link. Separate Link docs show Wallet settings and eligible transaction filtering, and business, presentment, amount, customer location, subscription/recurrence restrictions, so the overview does not promise every method displays or succeeds. Shopify, Squarespace and Adobe Commerce are partner/app routes, without implementation or availability detail (new raw lines 64–96; related Link integration lines 7–16 and funding lines 40–52).

Main route: wiki/index.md line 7 to wiki/stripe-index.md lines 22–32, 729 and 770 to wiki/concepts/stripe-checkout.md lines 12–30 and 248–255 and wiki/concepts/stripe-payment-intents.md lines 12–28. The mapped `source-stripe-accept-a-payment.md` is canonically a different URL (line 5); its own November 20-line variant index lives at /payments/accept-a-payment (related raw lines 1–20). Keep its April implementation, current index, and dated decision overview provenance distinct. The mapped source only references the April online-payments overview at line 90, missing the substantial new retrieval route.
substantive_changes: The same online-payments URL is rewritten as a full decision guide, expanding Checkout Sessions versus Payment Intents into explicit operational/API and feature tables with tax integration, checkout lifecycle ownership, expiry and event distinctions. It preserves the earlier high-level Checkout Sessions recommendation and Adaptive Pricing distinction while adding concrete responsibility and feature comparisons (old raw lines 6–20, new raw lines 29–62).

The new suite scope names the recommended full page, separately routed prebuilt embedded form, Checkout studio for creation/configuration/monitoring and payment method controls with Private preview qualification, and React Native Mobile Payment Element at this URL (old raw lines 14–20, new raw lines 13–27 and 64–76). This is new decision/navigation coverage in this overview, not a first launch claim. The already mapped April implementation describes React Native separately (source lines 54–62).

The November guide adds payment-method tools, specific saved Link methods and Instant Bank Payments/Klarna, Web/Mobile Link routes and Shopify/Squarespace/Adobe Commerce partner routes (new raw lines 64–96). Separate linked-leg implementation remains outside the overview. The old explicit account signup prerequisite and earlier no-code subscriber/quote/invoice/in-person/tip navigation drop out (old raw lines 12 and 22–32); omission supplies no evidence of waiver or feature removal.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Keep the April 20 account signup/Dashboard and no-code product discovery wording dated, plus the old Payments/Elements/iOS/Android routing. Preserve the HTML/React Checkout Sessions Elements example’s Session `client_secret`, Checkout initializer/provider, and Checkout confirmation as dated implementation details, distinct from the separate PaymentIntent client secret and `stripe.confirmPayment` flow already scoped at source lines 21–31. Treat the old agent-directed text as captured content, without carrying it forward as operational instructions (old raw lines 8–32).

Title, presentation, sectional reorganization, unchanged demo link, and changed quickstart/Payment Links URLs are presentation/navigation. The new topic-level descriptions and decision tables are substantive documentation coverage, without inferring API/SDK changes from a link, deployable configuration, or connected-business availability (old raw lines 4–20, new raw lines 5–27).

Keep the mapped Accept a Payment implementation and historical state caveats, including completed PaymentSheet and completed Checkout Session versus successful payment, sandbox versus live outcomes, historical consent/saving and customer-specific account details, as separate source evidence (mapped source lines 15–73).
conflicts: The online-payments page labels a distinct ‘Embedded form’ linking to the Form quickstart while its compressed table groups full page, embedded form and Elements. The separately captured Form quickstart declares `ui_mode=form` (related lines 35–50), while the separate Accept a Payment index's ‘Full embedded page’ uses a URL selector `ui=embedded-page` (index lines 13–16), and API create lines 518–531 distinguishes `embedded_page`, `form`, `elements`, and `hosted_page`. `2026-03-25.dahlia` separately replaces `hosted`/`embedded`/`custom` with the corresponding `hosted_page`/`embedded_page`/`elements` values and adds `form` (Dahlia changelog lines 5–28). Scope these routes and examples reciprocally in Checkout, Checkout Sessions and the mapped source rather than treating page labels or old examples as one wire enum.

November overview line 61's 24-hour expiry is scoped as the API default, not an immutable timer. The separate Checkout Session `expires_at` bounds are 30 minutes to 24 hours; PaymentIntents does not inherit this Session expiry. November line 62's comparative webhook row and Checkout completion do not prove a successful authorization, paid status, or captured funds. Use the mapped source's distinct paid/async fulfillment states and Session object `payment_status` vs `status` reference. The receipt comparison at line 59 concerns integrated order/receipt behavior, not absence of all PaymentIntent receipt tooling (separate PaymentIntent create API lines 665–668).

Checkout studio is Private preview in the parent page at lines 27 and 70. A separately captured product page confirms Dashboard workflows (lines 7–16) and does not turn the preview into a generally available capability or remove programming for unrelated integrations.

Do not relabel this 96-line same-URL overview as the separately scoped 20-line Accept a Payment base variant index, or treat a UI/API link or examples as updated underlying implementation. The mapped source's line 90 historical reference and line 15 own-canonical summary both remain valid for their dates and page identities.
unresolved_questions: This overview does not give site-specific access or runtime outcomes, the user's deployed API and SDK versions, or implement each linked product. The linked variant bodies of the separate Accept a Payment index were not read for this job.

findings: Add a clearly labeled full November /payments/online-payments comparison and discovery route beside the April /payments/online-payments raw pointer at line 90. Preserve /payments/accept-a-payment canonical ownership, its November variant index, and April full implementation provenance (source lines 5–9, 15–31 and 83–90).
Make API selection, the distinct UI/mobile/private-preview paths, dynamic method controls, Link and partner discovery, and expiry/event boundaries retrievable (new raw lines 9–96).
conflicts: Link Checkout Form separately from full embedded page and custom Elements, and use the Dahlia/API/quickstart evidence for actual enum and version scope. Qualify 24 hours as the default and preserve settlement/fulfillment boundaries. The current mapped source documents the other canonical page as an index, which does not describe this full overview.
source_assessments.reason: A reader looking for the November Stripe integration decision, newer dashboard and UI routes, or capabilities owned by the merchant on PaymentIntents finds only an April overview link. Label both identities so readers neither treat the 96-line overview as an implementation guide nor confuse it with the separate 20-line Accept a Payment index.

answers.Q1: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/online-payments, the November 7 guide describes the Optimized Checkout Suite’s payment UIs, dynamic payment methods and Link. It names no-code Payment Links without a website, the recommended full-page Checkout experience embedded or redirected on a merchant site, a separate prebuilt embedded form, custom Elements, Mobile Payment Element on iOS, Android and React Native, and Dashboard Checkout studio in Private preview (new raw lines 5-27). The April overview already described Payment Links, hosted and embedded Checkout, Elements, iOS and Android and explicitly required Stripe signup (old raw lines 8-20). Both favor Checkout Sessions for most integrations. November distinguishes basic `price_data` collection and fuller Session-owned checkout with built-in Stripe Tax, shipping, discounts, subscriptions, Adaptive Pricing, address/order tools and dynamic updates from the lower-level PaymentIntent route where the merchant computes the amount and owns checkout logic, integrating Tax and Subscriptions separately as needed. It contrasts default 24-hour Session expiry and checkout lifecycle events with PaymentIntent's lack of automatic Session expiry and payment-state tracking. Session completion is distinct from paid status (new raw lines 29-62, and separate Session object reference lines 312-322 and 368-378). Dynamic payment methods, eligibility rules, configurations and A/B tests are decision tools. Link reuses saved credit/debit cards or U.S. bank accounts and names Instant Bank Payments and Klarna, with separate Checkout/web/mobile routes and eligible transaction conditions. Shopify, Squarespace and Adobe Commerce are discovery routes (new raw lines 64-96). `source-stripe-accept-a-payment.md` currently covers the distinct `/payments/accept-a-payment` index and April implementation and only links this overview's April-dated predecessor at line 90.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/online-payments, the substantive change is fuller strategy coverage: the UI, API and feature comparisons, private-preview Checkout studio, payment method controls, Link and partner routes (old raw lines 8-32 and new raw lines 13-96). Title, layout, demo link and changed quickstart targets are presentation or navigation. Keep the April signup statement, no-code subscriber/invoice/in-person/donation links and HTML/React Checkout Sessions client-secret and confirmation example dated (old raw lines 8-32). November’s omission does not waive signup or remove those products. In `source-stripe-accept-a-payment.md` and the reciprocal Checkout and Payment Intents routes, keep this full comparison separate from the November 20-line `/payments/accept-a-payment` navigation index and the April implementation. The new prebuilt embedded form link and the separate full embedded page are distinct: the captured Form quickstart uses `ui_mode=form`, and the separate `2026-03-25.dahlia` change and current API reference distinguish `form`, `embedded_page`, `elements` and `hosted_page`. The label alone supplies no wire value or rollout proof (new raw lines 17-27 and new raw lines 39-57). Keep Stripe’s default 24-hour Session expiry qualified by API `expires_at` with a 30-minute-to-24-hour range, and distinguish Session completion, PaymentIntent state and paid fulfillment (new raw lines 59-62). Linking a mobile, Link, preview or partner route supplies discovery and documented intent. It does not prove deployed version, registration/eligibility, available payment methods for a given shopper, or successful payment.
